key_insight: Enforcing linear completeness in PIML removes a key obstacle to mesh-refinement convergence and supports rigorous H1 and L2 error estimates.
engineering_relevance: The approach can accelerate substructure-based finite element analysis while preserving conformity and improving convergence reliability.
method: Train neural networks to map material distributions or element geometries to substructure numerical shape functions.
Reconstruct transition-matrix columns using linear displacement constraints to ensure linear completeness.
Bound numerical error through finite element discretization and network generalization errors.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments verify the theoretical results and demonstrate optimal convergence rates, good generalization performance, and numerical stability.
watch_item: Linear completeness addresses convergence consistency, but practical accuracy still depends on network generalization to the target materials and geometries.
paper_title: Convergence and error analysis of problem-independent machine learning (PIML) with linear completeness
